To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the ratio of M1 mRNA to M2 mRNA increases 2.7 times during infection, the half-lives of both M1 and M 2 mRNA are 2.7 h, the kinetics of nucleo-cytoplasmic transport are the same for both M1 and mRNA and the kinetics of mRNA synthesis are similar for both M1 mRNA and M2 mRNA.

the efficiency of splicing of the influenza virus M1 gene changes during the course of an infection, that the splicing of M1 mRNA is regulated by a cellular mechanism, and that the regulation of M1 mRNA spicing occurs in the nucleus.
the ratio of M1 mRNA to M2 mRNA in influenza virus-inflected cells increases during the course of the infection and this change is due to an increase in splicing efficiency.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms by which influenza virus controls the expression of its genes.
the mechanisms of viral RNA splicing and the control of splicing efficiency.
the regulation of mRNA splicing during influenza virus infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ratio of M1 mRNA to M2 mRNA is regulated during infection by the splicing efficiency of M1 mRNA.
the splicing efficiency of M1 mRNA is regulated during influenza virus infection.
influenza virus RNA splicing is regulated in infected cells and that the regulation is at least partly at the level of intron removal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the splicing of M1 mRNA to M2 mRNA and M3 mRNA is regulated in a manner that is dependent upon the level of viral gene expression.
influenza virus regulates the ratio of M1 and mRNA3 by a mechanism which is dependent on the time in infection.
influenza virus regulates the ratio of M1 and 2 mRNAs by a change in the splicing efficiency of M1 mRNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the regulation of influenza viral RNA splicing is a highly regulated and complex process.
influenza virus-infected mammalian cells have the capacity to modulate the ratio of two closely related mRNA species in a regulated manner.
influenza viral RNA splicing is regulated and that the splicing efficiency changes about 20 times over the course of infection.
